 Put your bids in to acquire Corey Kiner from the waiver wire. Michael Owens / Getty Images 
 By Michael Salfino Nov. 10, 2026 Updated Share article 12 The trading deadline didn’t provide the splash we expected, though the Minnesota Vikings made a much-needed move. The 49ers added a veteran to shore up the receiver room, but there’s someone I’m more excited about in San Francisco than Keenan Allen.
 Target and touch totals are important, but not as important as the market share. “Targets” is mostly a receiver stat (although there are some notable exceptions). Touches are the currency of the running back.
 Advertisement
 What we’re doing is really simple. For pass-catchers, market share is targets divided by team pass attempts. For running backs, it is touches divided by team plays from scrimmage (not team touches, to be clear).
 Snap counts and depth of target and type of touch (running back receptions are way more valuable than RB carries) are also important but generally will not be discussed here. This is pure market share. Consider this a primary tool for assessing waivers and trades.
 Here’s the list . Be sure to select the current week but all the weeks of the season will be archived so you can get a multi-week sample on a player if you so desire. Also note as the season progresses that I gave great thought in doing these stats weekly and not for the season. The objective here is to respond quickly to present trends. Yearly stats just smoothes everything out to a more meaningless middle. Remember, as our Gene McCaffrey so wisely says, “To be very right, you have to be willing to be very wrong.”
 Touches
 The top waiver-wire pickup based on injuries and the model is New England's Corey Kiner. You combine his usage with the injured Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, week-to-week) and you get about 28%, which would track at about 17th. And then you add a good offense with a top QB (Drake Maye), so you expect Kiner to outperform that market-share ranking. Week-to-week with a knee sounds to me like about three weeks for Stevenson (Lions, bye, Chargers), and it could mean more. I’d bid 25%, and I bet that gets him 75% of the time.
 Next for me is Audric Estime. This depends on the status of Travis Etienne, who didn’t return from his hamstring injury after the bye. I’d bet Estime runs it back this week (Panthers) and maybe next, and then who knows after that. Maybe a 15% bid?
 Similarly, you can bet that Josh Jacobs misses this week after surgery to repair a broken finger and then there’s a bye and a short week. Do you want to play Kaleb Johnson against the Vikings? I don’t. Then you have a bye, the Rams (not a good matchup) and 10 days before the Saints (great matchup, but Jacobs will definitely be back then given his injury was reportedly three weeks, max).
 It’s basically Kiner or bust for me. I’d put Estime on the block as a backup.
 Advertisement
 As I wrote Sunday night , I love Jonah Coleman’s usage (No. 10), and he survived the trade deadline.
 Breece Hall resumed the No. 1 role in the Jets' RB committee. He should be traded because, while he’s good, Braelon Allen is better and may be great. Allen is also still just 22 years old.
 Zach Charbonnet was No. 17, which would make him an RB2. If I squint really hard I can sort of see it. I think Jadarian Price is better at the moment, given Charbonnet may not be 100% until 2027 due to his ACL surgery.
 Saquon Barkley at No. 30 is borderline unplayable given he’s nearly 30 years old and seems washed.
 Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones continue to split 30% market share in an offense that should be less brutal with Cousins under center.
 I think Kaelon Black is a low-end starter at the moment, in the same bucket as Kenneth Gainwell; however, Black would be amazing with an injury to Christian McCaffrey.
 Targets
 My top pick this week didn’t even chart, since he didn’t meet the required threshold of five targets. He caught all four of his targets for 84 yards and a 37-yard TD. That would be Jordan Watkins. I do not think Mike Evans will be back for weeks given Achilles tendinitis is typically a 6-10-week injury (see 2024 Christian McCaffrey), and maybe that's why the 49ers traded for Allen.
 DeMarcus Robinson is 32 years old and has never been good. Deebo Samuel is a gadget receiver. Watkins ran a 4.35 40-yard dash, and, though he never earned targets, he could be Matthew Golden-like in suddenly earning them now and really opening up this offense. Brock Purdy is also great, and Watkins is best positioned, I believe, to ride that wave.
 Heading the waiver-wire options based on usage in Week 9 are No. 12 Caleb Douglas, No. 18 Makai Lemon, No. 19 Darren Waller, No. 25 Tank Dell and No. 28 Tre' Harris. Nothing thrilling there, and I’m not including Omar Cooper (No. 9) since I assume he is gone in your league.
 Advertisement
 From that waiver-wire group, Dell and Waller are the only two deserving a bid. The Texans have turned into the pre-2026, post-Aaron Rodgers Packers. They throw downfield and they have a ton of options that get in each other’s way. Everyone is playable, but no one is remotely bettable. Nico Collins didn’t even chart this week. It’s great for C.J. Stroud, but it’s hard to navigate such a wide passing tree. Still, Dell just did it. He showed he is explosive. He earned the most targets on the team. I’d be in there on waivers, but I’d bid conservatively. I don’t think there will be a stampede to get Dell, though I’d like to add him.
 Waller was one of just nine players with 10+ targets in Week 9. He’s been spotty when it comes to usage, but his usage correlates with Jalen Coker's, it seems. As Coker goes, so does Waller. If Coker's targets are sparse, Waller probably does something. If the Panthers focus on the wide receivers in the passing game, Waller is going to be quiet. (In Week 9, Tetairoa McMillan was No. 62 overall and Jalen Coker No. 74.)
 Caleb Douglas and Lemon have too many QB problems for me to be interested, and the Chargers/Harris are just a disaster — I can’t proactively play a Charger even if Ladd McConkey is out a while.
 DeMario Douglas looked a lot better in raw targets than in market share, but I think we’re looking at WR30 or so as a ceiling, with basically no floor. Tight end Eli Raridon is the Patriots pass catcher I think will pop in the second half. Yes, Hunter Henry is in the way, but the Patriots traditionally have been a two-TE offense, and they should be using that as their base offense, in my opinion. As I said last week, at WR, I’d take Efton Chism III for nothing if you agree with me that A.J. Brown will be out for a while.
